title: The past simple
subtitle: Finished actions in the past
review: Written by Claude in the format of the French tense pages. Check the examples and the level.
intro: Use it for something that **started and finished in the past**. We often say **when**: *yesterday, last week, in 2020, two days ago*. It is the tense of **stories**.

blocks.label: One finished action
blocks.title: It happened, and it is over

examples.fr: She **bought** a new bag last week.
I **got** up, **washed** my face and **ate** breakfast.

blocks.label: Past habits
blocks.title: Again and again, but not now

examples.fr: When I was little, I **walked** to school every day.
We **played** in the river every summer.
My grandfather **told** us a story every night.
He **had** a small dog when he was a boy.
We **lived** in a village for ten years.

blocks.title: Regular verbs
points:
Short verb, one vowel + one consonant: **double** the last letter
*stop* → *stopped*, *plan* → *planned*, *clap* → *clapped*.
blocks.note: *I played, you played, she played, they played*: there is no -s in the past.

blocks.title: Irregular verbs
blocks.text: Many common verbs do **not** take -ed. You have to learn them.

blocks.title: The verb be
blocks.formula: I / he / she / it **was**   ·   you / we / they **were**

blocks.text: yesterday, last night / week / month / year, two days ago, a long time ago, in 2020, on Monday, this morning (when the morning is over), when I was little, then, after that …

blocks.note: After *didn't*, use the **base verb**: *I didn't go*, not *I didn't went*.

examples.en: Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.

examples.fr: **Were** you at school yesterday? **Was** it cold?
examples.en: With be, put was or were first.

examples.fr: **Past simple**: a finished time. *I lost my pen yesterday.*
examples.en: We know when. The story is in the past.

examples.fr: **Present perfect**: no time, and it matters now. *I have lost my pen.*
examples.en: I do not have it now.

examples.fr: **Not together**: *I have seen him yesterday.* ✗  →  *I saw him yesterday.* ✓
examples.en: With yesterday, last week, ago: always the past simple.
